text: 2     Lecture1B CS294-277 Fall 2024                                                                 Lecturer: Jitendra Malik September 9, 2024                                                          Scribe: Chung Min Kim, Brent Yi Lecture 1B: Biomechanics of Walking and Running Abstract These notes summarize key concepts from Lecture 1B of CS294-277, based on “The Science of Sports, Robotics, and Rehabilitation" by Uchida and Delp. 2.1    Walking 2.2    Gait Cycle The gait cycle of walking consists of two main phases: the stance phase and the swing phase. The stance phase includes foot contact, foot flat, heel off, and toe off. The swing phase involves peak knee flexion and ends with foot contact. A key characteristic of walking is that at least one foot is always on the ground, which distinguishes it from running, where both feet can be in the air. This is also the definition of running in the Olympics. 2.3    Basic Concepts A stride is defined as the distance between two consecutive foot contacts of the same foot. The normal stride length for an adult is approximately 1.2-1.4 meters, although this can vary depending on the individual. The average walking speed is about 4.5 km/h
